national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), principally through the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE). Business formalities are filed through the national Guichet unique operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI); tax services and filings are accessible through impots.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS is registered through the INPI Guichet unique. The registration process results in allocation of a SIREN and establishment-specific SIRET by INSEE and registration in the applicable register. The company must provide its registration details to the competent SIE and obtain or confirm its French intra-Community VAT number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire), generally composed of the FR country prefix, a two-character key, and the SIREN. A foreign entity without a French establishment that makes French taxable supplies must contact the competent SIE for foreign businesses and apply for French VAT registration before commencing transactions requiring registration. A non-EU-established taxable person generally must appoint a French tax representative unless an applicable legal exception or mutual-assistance arrangement applies. VAT registration does not itself create a permanent establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is generally subject to French corporation tax (impôt sur les sociétés, or IS). It may elect the temporary partnership tax regime under Article 239 bis AB of the French Tax Code for up to five fiscal years if all statutory conditions are met, including qualifying ownership, activity, age, size, and non-listing requirements; profits are then taxed at shareholder level under the applicable rules. This is not a general US-style check-the-box election. No general election permits a SAS to select an arbitrary hybrid classification for French tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT; taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, or TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a France-established SAS supplying goods, the domestic small-business VAT exemption (franchise en base) generally applies only while annual turnover remains within the applicable goods threshold, commonly EUR 85,000, subject to statutory threshold, prior-year, current-year, and transition rules. A separate, lower threshold applies to services. The exemption is not a general registration safe harbor for non-established suppliers or transactions for which VAT registration is otherwise required. The SAS should verify the thresholds in force for the relevant tax year and transaction type.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is introducing phased domestic electronic invoicing and transaction-reporting obligations. Under the current timetable, all in-scope businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; issuing obligations begin on that date for large and intermediate-sized enterprises and are scheduled to begin on 1 September 2027 for SMEs and micro-enterprises. In-scope invoices must be transmitted through an approved platform under the statutory system, with separate electronic reporting for relevant transactions outside domestic B2B e-invoicing, including certain B2C and cross-border transactions. France does not generally require real-time tax-authority clearance or digital fiscal stamping of each invoice. Businesses should confirm current implementation rules and applicable exemptions before deployment.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from France to a destination outside the European Union may be exempt from French VAT with a right to deduct input VAT, subject to the French Tax Code conditions and proof that the goods actually left the EU. Intra-Community supplies of goods may be exempt only where the statutory conditions are met, including dispatch to another Member State, a valid customer VAT number, and required recapitulative reporting. Services are not zero-rated merely because the customer is offshore: place-of-supply rules determine whether French VAT applies, and specific exemptions may apply. For die-cast model exports, retain evidence linking the sale, goods, customs export, and transport to the non-EU destination.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration and MRN, with electronic confirmation of exit from the EU customs territory
Commercial invoice, customer order or contract, and records identifying the exported goods and quantities
Bill of lading, air waybill, courier record, or other transport documentation linking the goods to the destination outside the EU
Proof of delivery or other reliable evidence of receipt at the non-EU destination, where available
Accounting records and payment evidence; an inward remittance certificate is not a general French statutory prerequisite for export VAT exemption
For qualifying intra-Community supplies rather than exports outside the EU: customer VAT-number verification, transport evidence, and required EU sales-list reporting
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No general French foreign-exchange repatriation deadline applies to export proceeds. If export exemption is unsupported or the goods did not leave the EU, the DGFiP may assess output VAT, deny or recover related deductions or refunds, and charge late-payment interest. Tax penalties may apply for omissions, inaccurate returns, deliberate breaches, or fraud; fraudulent conduct may also trigger enhanced penalties and criminal proceedings under applicable law. The taxpayer must retain sufficient contemporaneous evidence and produce it during an audit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF), operating within the Eurosystem framework and the European Central Bank (ECB); primary supervisory authority for credit institutions and payment services is the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution), with BdF overseeing the balance-of-payments and external financial reporting regime under the Code monétaire et financier (CMF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France applies full current-account and capital-account convertibility for the euro pursuant to TFEU Article 63 and CMF Articles L151-1 et seq. There are no exchange controls preventing profit remittance, dividend distribution, or liquidation proceeds repatriation to non-resident shareholders. For a French SAS, profit remittance requires a valid shareholder distribution decision, statutory auditor certificate where applicable, and French withholding tax compliance (12.5% standard, treaty-reduced where applicable). Foreign direct investment into non-licensed sectors such as ISIC 3240 (die-cast model manufacturing) by non-EU investors is not subject to prior authorisation, only a prior administrative declaration under CMF Article L151-3; the capital injection is freely bankable once the declaration is filed with the Ministry of Economy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds exists in France. Exporters may freely retain the full invoice value in foreign currency current accounts held with French licensed banks for an indefinite period. The only binding obligation is statistical: all cross-border flows must be reported to the Banque de France under EU Regulation (EC) No 184/2005 and French CMF Articles R152-4 et seq., typically via the resident bank's OFI (Observation des Finances Internationales) reporting, on a monthly or quarterly basis depending on counterparty and transaction size.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM – Legal constraints are material. A non-EU offshore digital EMI (e.g., UK, Singapore, US) cannot lawfully provide payment accounts to a French-domiciled treasury entity without an ACPR licence, a French branch licence, or an EU passport under PSD2 (Directive (EU) 2015/2366). EU-licensed EMIs (e.g., Qonto, Shine, N26) may on-board the SAS remotely and are adequate for EUR-denominated operational cash management; however, they generally lack robust SWIFT MT103 outbound clearing to Chinese suppliers and are not accepted as a primary escrow bank by commercial counterparties. Recommended use: secondary operating account only; primary escrow relationship must sit with a Tier 1 full-service bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is legally permissible under ACPR guidance if the bank applies an endorsed video-KYC procedure (live identity verification). However, Tier 1 French banks in practice require at least one physical or videoconference interview with the SAS Président and, for non-EU shareholders, notarised apostilled corporate documents. A physical appointment at a Paris banking centre is strongly recommended for the initial on-boarding; subsequent account signatories may be on-boarded remotely via video. Non-French residency of directors is not a statutory blocker but materially increases documentary scrutiny.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) is a resident of a FATF high-risk or monitored jurisdiction, or presents a thin verifiable digital footprint.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised French UBO declaration (Cerfa form 16025), certified and apostilled passport copies, certified proof of residential address, 3-year corporate registry extract of the shareholder entity, bank reference letters from two prior institutions, and a source-of-wealth declaration supported by 3 years of tax returns or audited financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions list or negative-media fuzzy match on a director's name, common with romanised Chinese pinyin names.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified PFAC (Personne Politiquement Exposée / sanctions) clearance search from the EU Commission consolidated sanctions list and the French Treasury list, formal legal opinion letter from a licensed French avocat attesting to the absence of name identity, sworn affidavit of name-alias independence, and a government-issued ID displaying the exact tonal romanisation used on the corporate registry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection exceeding EUR 50,000 from a related non-resident shareholder without a clear economic and legal basis for the contribution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAS shareholders' meeting minutes formally approving the capital increase, share subscription agreement with ISIC 3240 business plan, bank statements showing lawful origin of funds, notarised wire-instruction authenticity certificate, and the completed declaration of foreign direct investment filed with the Ministry of Economy (CMF Article L151-3) where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring low-value disbursements to multiple Chinese die-casting suppliers (more than 10 counterparties per month) generating suspicion of transaction structuring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full set of ISIC 3240 supply agreements and purchase orders, French customs import declarations (DAU), Bills of Lading and air-waybills, freight forwarder reconciliation reports, supplier factory-bank account confirmation letters, and a price-list consistency letter from the die-cast parts manufacturer establishing genuine trade compulsion.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: non-resident shareholder instructs SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for serial transfers) to the SAS escrow account held at the French Tier 1 bank. Field 70 (Remittance Information) must carry the Banque de France balance-of-payments category code for equity capital, typically 'C4 – Shares and other equity (capital injection)', plus the descriptive phrase 'APPORT EN CAPITAL FR_SAS' and the notarial or board resolution reference. The receiving bank will require a certified copy of the shareholders' meeting minutes and, if the beneficial owner is non-EU, evidence of the prior administrative declaration to the Ministry of Economy. Funds should be denominated in EUR; any USD or CNY inflow will trigger FX conversion and mandatory BdF statistical reporting by the bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For payments to Chinese die-casting suppliers, the standard clearing rails are: (1) SWIFT MT103 for direct corporate wire transfers, with the purpose code disclosed in field 70 referencing the underlying purchase contract (e.g., 'GRANT OF USE – IMPORT TRADE PAYMENT / CONTRACT N°'); (2) Commercial Documentary Letter of Credit (L/C at sight or usance) opened via SWIFT MT700 for larger, staged deliveries under Incoterms 2020 (FOB/CIF), acceptable to most PRC banks; (3) SEPA Credit Transfer (SEPA-CT) solely for EUR-denominated payments to counterparties within the SEPA zone, which is not applicable to China. All outbound wires are subject to the bank's OFI reporting and anti-money-laundering screening; the client must maintain a complete 'pièce justificative' file including invoice, packing list, customs export documents, and shipping evidence for at least five years.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/CNY outright forward contract (up to 12 months tenor) transacted with the Tier 1 bank's treasury desk without requiring an ISDA master agreement where the notional amount is under the bank's standard corporate limit and the transaction is backed by a real trade invoice under ISIC 3240.
EUR/USD vanilla FX swap (short-dated 1–6 months) for managing working-capital currency mismatches between USD-denominated sales revenue and EUR-denominated operating expenses.

CNH/CNY non-deliverable forward (NDF) to hedge RMB volatility when the underlying purchase contract from the Chinese die-casting factory is invoiced in CNY and the French entity's functional currency is EUR; settlement is in EUR on a net basis.
Cross-currency swap (EUR vs USD) executed via the bank treasury desk, restricted to notional amounts not exceeding 150% of forecast annual trade exposure with Chinese and eurozone counterparties.

Listed FX futures (EUR/USD and EUR/CNH) cleared through a French clearing member, used exclusively for pre-export hedging of committed purchase orders and subject to strict board-approved hedging policy with no speculative trading mandate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts (comptes annuels) comprising balance sheet, profit and loss statement, annexe, and confidentiality declaration (déclaration de confidentialité) if claimed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (competent commercial court registry), via the electronic national register portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval of annual accounts within 6 months of fiscal year-end; deposit with the registry within 1 month of approval, generally no later than 31 July for a 31 December fiscal year-end in the absence of a court-ordered extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to EUR 1,500 for individuals and EUR 7,500 for legal entities; court-ordered injunction to file subject to astreinte (coercive daily penalty) up to EUR 300 per day; two consecutive years of non-filing triggers provisional strike-off (radiation provisoire), leading to definitive strike-off after continued non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a commissaire aux comptes for any SAS exceeding at least two of the following thresholds at year-end: total balance sheet assets greater than EUR 4,000,000; net turnover greater than EUR 8,000,000; average regular headcount greater than 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général per Autorité des Normes Comptables Regulation 2018-01); statutory accounts in euros and French language; consolidated accounts may apply EU IFRS when consolidation thresholds are met.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone annual UBO revalidation filing in France. The beneficial-owner declaration (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs) is filed at incorporation and updated within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership. The annual accounts filing triggers registry verification of the existing UBO record; discrepancies must be remedied by a corrected certified UBO declaration.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des mouvements de titres (securities movement register evidencing share transfer history)
Registre des délibérations et décisions des associés (minutes and written decision register maintained at the registered office)
Registre de documentation juridique (legal document file for credentials, agreements, and règlementées conventions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 280 - USD 690 per year (commercial domiciliation service, excluding physical office lease overheads)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500 - USD 12,000 per year for a mid-size SAS statutory audit; higher for consolidated or multi-entity scopes
